claims.text: HEA multilayers with coherent interfaces can enable a transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep mechanisms.
The creep-mechanism transition is enabled by the ability of coherent-interface HEA multilayers to accommodate dislocation glide and diffusion at high temperatures.
Interface coherency is the structural mediator governing creep behavior.
Dislocation glide and diffusion accommodation constitute the proposed creep mechanism.
Increasing temperature and interface coherency will cause a transition from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
Incoherent-interface HEA multilayers provide the baseline for comparison.
Temperature defines a range within which the creep mechanisms transition.
Temperature-controlled in situ TEM can be used to observe dislocation dynamics and interface coherency in HEA multilayers.
The quantitative relationship between interface coherency and the creep-mechanism transition is unknown.
